mainTopic: Where does רבי מאיר learn that on ערב פסח one may burn pure תרומה together with impure תרומה? Interpreting the word ״מדבריהם״ in the משנה.
overview: The משנה quotes רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים: the כהנים burned meat made impure by a ולד הטומאה together with meat made impure by an אב הטומאה. Then רבי מאיר says that ״מדבריהם״ (from their words) we learn that on ערב פסח one may burn pure תרומה together with impure תרומה. The amud opens by finishing the first explanation, in which ״מדבריהם״ means רבי חנינא's words. ריש לקיש, quoting בר קפרא, disagrees. He says רבי חנינא's case involves impurities that are both Torah-level, so רבי מאיר's source must be a ruling of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. The גמרא first suggests their dispute about a barrel of uncertain תרומה. It rejects that source, because there רבי יהושע only allows indirect causing (גרמא), not making it impure by hand (בידים). It then settles on their dispute about a barrel of תרומה that broke in the upper winepress, where רבי יהושע allows making the תרומה impure by hand. It explains that the plural ״מדבריהם״ fits because the lesson comes from their dispute, and our משנה itself later names these two Sages. רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, says the same. רבא then challenges him by quoting רבי יוסי's ברייתא: רבי יוסי accepts burning impure תרומה with more severely impure תרומה, but refuses to burn doubtful תרומה with impure תרומה, since אליהו might come and declare it pure. The point of רבא's challenge is spelled out on the next amud.

steps.title: The previous explanation wraps up: ״their words" means רבי חנינא
steps.stepSummary: The previous approach closes by defining ״מדבריהם״ in the משנה as the words of רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does "from their words" mean? From the words of רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the explanation it just gave. It says that when רבי מאיר says ״from their words," he means the words of רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים quoted earlier in the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this approach, רבי מאיר builds his ruling about burning pure and impure תרומה together directly on רבי חנינא's statement in our משנה. This is the end of that approach. The next step brings a different opinion that disagrees about what ״מדבריהם״ refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: "From their words" – רבי מאיר's phrase in the משנה naming the source of his ruling
The deputy כהן גדול
The תנא in the משנה who describes how the כהנים burned impure meat

phrases.english: And what does "from their words" mean?
phrases.notes: Refers to רבי מאיר's phrase in the משנה.

phrases.english: From the words of Rabbi Chanina, the deputy High Priest.
phrases.notes: His statement appears earlier in the same משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the explanation given on the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Under the first approach, רבי מאיר's source is רבי חנינא's statement in our משנה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: both impurities are Torah-level, so ״their words" means רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, quoting בר קפרא, says רבי חנינא's case involves an אב הטומאה and a ולד הטומאה that are both דאורייתא. Therefore ״מדבריהם״ refers to רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said in the name of בר קפרא: Our משנה is about an אב הטומאה that is impure by Torah law and a ולד הטומאה that is impure by Torah law. And what does "from their words" mean? From the words of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a new explanation. He says רבי חנינא was talking about things that are impure by Torah law. Because of that, רבי מאיר could not have learned his ruling from רבי חנינא, so ״from their words" must refer to a ruling of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע found elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי חנינא's case, meat that is already impure becomes more impure. רבי מאיר's case is different: pure תרומה becomes impure. Since the cases do not match, ריש לקיש says רבי מאיר is relying on a different source, a ruling of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. The גמרא now has to find that source.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא from ארץ ישראל, the student-colleague of רבי יוחנן
A sage from the transition between the תנאים and the אמוראים
A primary source of impurity
A secondary source of impurity, made impure by an אב הטומאה
By Torah law

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not saying רבי חנינא is irrelevant to the משנה. He is only saying that רבי מאיר's word ״מדבריהם״ points to a different source.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said in the name of Bar Kappara:
Our Mishnah is about a primary source of impurity by Torah law
and a secondary source of impurity by Torah law.
And what does "from their words" mean?
From the words of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua.
phrases.notes: A ruling of theirs found elsewhere.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of ״מדבריהם״ from the approach that just ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא's case is about Torah-level impurities, and רבי מאיר's source is the words of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new path. It ties רבי מאיר's ruling to a dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. The גמרא will settle on their dispute about the barrel of תרומה that broke in the winepress (steps 7-8), not their dispute about uncertain תרומה.

steps.title: Which statement of רבי יהושע is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which ruling of רבי יהושע ריש לקיש means, and begins to propose a משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which ruling of רבי יהושע? If you say it is this ruling of רבי יהושע, as we learned in a משנה:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which ruling of רבי יהושע ריש לקיש is pointing to. It begins to suggest one. This is a setup line: the next steps quote the משנה being suggested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אילימא ("if you say") signals a first guess that the גמרא will test, and often reject. דתנן introduces a quotation from a משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Which?
"If you say" – introduces a suggestion that will be tested
"As we learned in a משנה"

steps.confusionAlert: אילימא usually means the suggestion is about to be challenged. Do not treat it as the גמרא's final answer.

phrases.english: Which ruling of Rabbi Yehoshua?
If you say it is this ruling of Rabbi Yehoshua, as we learned in a Mishnah:

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ? אִילֵּימָא הָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact source ריש לקיש is pointing to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The specific ruling of רבי יהושע that רבי מאיר relies on.

steps.title: The barrel of uncertain תרומה: רבי אליעזר says protect it
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה is about a barrel of תרומה that developed a ספק טומאה. רבי אליעזר says one must still protect it from impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: A barrel of תרומה that developed an uncertain impurity: רבי אליעזר says, if it was resting in an exposed place, one should move it to a hidden place, and if it was uncovered, one should cover it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first half of the suggested משנה. רבי אליעזר rules that even when תרומה is only possibly impure, one must keep guarding it from becoming definitely impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since it is uncertain whether the תרומה is impure, it may not be eaten. But it is also not definitely impure, so רבי אליעזר holds that one may not cause it to become impure. Moving it to a safe spot and covering it are ways of protecting it.

keyTerms.meaning: A barrel
The portion of produce given to a כהן; it must be kept pure
Uncertain impurity
An exposed place where it could become impure
A hidden, protected place

phrases.english: A barrel of terumah
about which an uncertainty of impurity arose:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
If it was resting in an exposed place,
he should place it in a hidden place,
and if it was uncovered, he should cover it.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָבִית שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה שֶׁנּוֹלַד לָהּ סְפֵק טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the first half of the משנה proposed in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: Identifying the dispute ריש לקיש refers to.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a barrel of תרומה with a ספק טומאה (רבי אליעזר's view).

steps.title: רבי יהושע: no need to protect uncertain תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע rules that one may even move the barrel to an exposed place, or uncover it, since it no longer needs protection.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: If it was resting in a hidden place, he may place it in an exposed place, and if it was covered, he may uncover it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יהושע's view in the same משנה. He says there is no duty to guard uncertain תרומה, and one may even expose it to impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Uncertain תרומה can never be eaten. It can only be used for burning, for example as fuel. So רבי יהושע holds that one may let it become impure. Following the proposed link, the same reasoning would allow רבי מאיר's ruling: on ערב פסח, pure חמץ תרומה that must be destroyed anyway may be burned together with impure תרומה. The גמרא will test this proposed link next.

keyTerms.meaning: He may place it
Covered
He may uncover it

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש reads ״מדבריהם״ as pointing to the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. The candidate source is their dispute over uncertain תרומה: רבי אליעזר says guard it, and רבי יהושע says one may even expose it to impurity.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע is not saying the תרומה is definitely impure. It is still uncertain. His point is only that since it can never be eaten, there is no duty to protect it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
If it was resting in a hidden place,
he may place it in an exposed place,
and if it was covered, he may uncover it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted משנה with the opposing view.
steps.raayaObject: The proposed source for רבי מאיר's ruling.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע's lenient ruling about uncertain תרומה.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this identification holds, רבי מאיר's ruling about burning on ערב פסח would rest on רבי יהושע's principle that תרומה which can never be eaten need not be protected from impurity.

steps.title: Indirect causing is not the same as doing it with your hands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the barrel with a ספק טומאה. In that case רבי יהושע only allowed indirect causing of impurity (גרמא), but burning pure and impure תרומה together makes it impure directly (בידים).
steps.simpleTranslation: Are the cases really alike? There, it is only indirect causing. Here, it is done directly with one's hands!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof it just brought from the barrel case. The two cases do not match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the barrel case, putting the barrel in an exposed place only sets up a chance that it will become impure later. That is only גרמא, indirect causing. Burning pure תרומה together with impure תרומה makes the pure one impure right away, with your own action. So allowing גרמא does not prove that רבי יהושע would allow making something impure בידים.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it comparable? (a formula used to reject a comparison)
Indirect causation. You set things up, and the result happens on its own.
With one's hands. Direct, active causing.
There / here. Used to contrast two cases.

steps.confusionAlert: In this line, "הָתָם" (there) means the barrel case from steps 4-5. "הָכָא" (here) means burning pure and impure תרומה together on ערב פסח. Do not mix up which case is which.

phrases.english: Is it comparable?
There, it is merely indirect causation.
phrases.notes: The barrel with a ספק טומאה placed in an exposed spot.

phrases.english: Here, it is with one's hands!
phrases.notes: Burning pure and impure תרומה together makes the pure one impure directly.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי דָּמֵי? הָתָם — גְּרָמָא בְּעָלְמָא. הָכָא — בְּיָדַיִם!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source proposed in steps 4-5 as the basis for ״מדבריהם״.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the identification of the barrel-of-ספק-טומאה משנה as the source. ריש לקיש's basic claim is not rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proposed source allows only גרמא (indirect causing). The case of burning together involves direct impurity בידים.

steps.title: A new source: the barrel that broke in the winepress
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes a different ruling of רבי יהושע. It quotes a משנה about a barrel of תרומה wine that broke in the upper part of a winepress, while the lower part holds impure חולין wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is this ruling of רבי יהושע, as we learned in a משנה: a barrel of תרומה broke in the upper winepress, and in the lower one there is impure חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the first source, the גמרא offers a new one. It starts by describing the case in the משנה, which sets up the dispute in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תרומה wine is about to flow down into impure חולין wine. Once it does, it will become impure on its own. The mixture will also become impure תרומה, which no one may drink, so there is a big loss. This sets up a case where the תרומה is going to be lost anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Introduces a new suggestion after rejecting the old one.
As we learned in a משנה
Winepress
Impure non-sacred food (here, wine)

phrases.english: Rather, it is this ruling of Rabbi Yehoshua,
as we learned in a mishna:
a barrel of teruma wine
that broke in the upper winepress,
and in the lower one there is impure non-sacred wine,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source rejected in step 6 with a new one.
steps.raayaObject: Identifying which ruling of רבי יהושע ״מדבריהם״ refers to
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of the barrel of תרומה broken in the upper winepress

steps.title: רבי יהושע allows making the תרומה impure with one's hands
steps.stepSummary: Both agree that if a רביעית can be saved in purity, it must be saved. If not, רבי אליעזר says to let it flow down and become impure on its own, but רבי יהושע says one may even make it impure directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree that if one can save a רביעית of it in purity, he should save it. If not, רבי אליעזר says: let it flow down and become impure, but he should not make it impure with his hand. רבי יהושע says: he may even make it impure with his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the dispute. רבי יהושע allows making the תרומה impure directly, which is exactly what the גמרא needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the תרומה will become impure anyway, רבי יהושע lets a person make it impure with his own hand (for example, by catching it in impure vessels) to prevent a bigger loss. This matches burning pure and impure תרומה together on ערב פסח. The pure חמץ will be lost anyway, so making it impure directly is allowed. Unlike the barrel case of step 6, this is בידים.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees (both sides agree on this point)
A quarter-לוג, a set liquid measure
He should rescue it
Let it flow down and become impure on its own
He makes it impure with his hand, directly

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a case of direct impurity בידים for something that will be lost anyway. That is exactly what the case of burning together needs, so it fixes the problem raised in step 6.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua agree
that if one is able to rescue from it
a quarter-log in purity, he should rescue it.
And if not, Rabbi Eliezer says:
Let it descend and become impure,
but he should not make it impure with his hand.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
He may even make it impure with his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה begun in step 7 by giving the dispute and רבי יהושע's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: Shows that רבי יהושע allows direct impurity for תרומה that will be lost anyway
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע's ruling: אַף יְטַמְּאֶנָּה בַּיָּד

steps.title: Then it should say "from his words," not "from their words"
steps.stepSummary: If the source is only רבי יהושע's view, the plural ״מדבריהם״ does not fit. The text should have said ״מדבריו״, from his words.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this phrase "from their words" should have been "from his words"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new source by looking closely at the wording ״מדבריהם״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the winepress משנה, רבי אליעזר forbids making the תרומה impure by hand. So the lesson of burning together comes only from רבי יהושע. The plural "their words" suggests a lesson drawn from both תנאים, which this source does not provide.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a problem that follows from the last claim)
From his words (singular)
It should have said

steps.whatToRemember: The winepress משנה proves the הלכה (רבי יהושע allows direct impurity), but it does not seem to fit the plural wording ״מדבריהם״. The next step answers this: the lesson comes from the dispute of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע together.

phrases.english: If so,
this phrase "from their words,"
it should have said "from his words"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source proposed in steps 7-8 from the angle of the משנה's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: Identifying the winepress משנה as the source of ״מדבריהם״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural ״מדבריהם״ means a lesson drawn from both רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. Here only רבי יהושע's view supports burning together, so the text should read ״מדבריו״.

steps.title: Their words means the dispute of both Sages
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the plural problem: רבי מאיר means he learned the rule from the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי מאיר is saying: We learned it from the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9 about why the text says ״מדבריהם״ (plural). The source is the argument between two Sages, so the plural word fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling itself follows רבי יהושע, who allows making תרומה impure directly. But the lesson comes from the argument as a whole, because the two views side by side show the point. That is why רבי מאיר says 'from their words.'

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (a rereading of a statement)
A dispute between Sages
We learned

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: מִמַּחְלוֹקְתָּן שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: From the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua
we learned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording problem raised in step 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״מדבריהם״ seemed to point to only one Sage, so the plural did not fit
steps.terutzMaskana: ״מדבריהם״ refers to the dispute of both רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע

steps.title: The wording of the משנה supports this reading
steps.stepSummary: The rest of the משנה mentions both רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע, which supports reading ״מדבריהם״ as referring to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also exact, because the משנה goes on to say 'רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its answer from the wording of our משנה, the one where רבי מאיר says ״מדבריהם״. That משנה later mentions רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע by name. The גמרא then closes with 'learn from it,' meaning the answer is accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The דייקא comes from our own משנה in פסחים, not from the winepress משנה. Later in our משנה, after רבי מאיר's statement and רבי יוסי's reply, it says ״ומודים רבי אליעזר ורבי יהושע״. Since our משנה itself brings in these two Sages, it makes sense that רבי מאיר's 'their words' points to them. The point is then accepted with שמע מינה.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also exact (supports the reading)
Agrees, concedes
Learn from it (the point is accepted)

phrases.english: It is also precise:
as it teaches: 'Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua agree.'
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 10 from the text of the משנה
steps.raayaObject: That ״מדבריהם״ refers to רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה continues with 'מודה רבי אליעזר ורבי יהושע'
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר learned his rule from the dispute of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. That is why he says 'their words' in the plural.

steps.title: רב נחמן holds the same view
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, says the earlier testimonies deal with Torah-level impurity. He also explains ״מדבריהם״ as the words of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so said רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה: The case in the משנה deals with an אב הטומאה from the Torah and a ולד הטומאה from the Torah. And what does 'from their words' mean? From the words of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an אמורא who says the same thing. רב נחמן explains which kind of impurity the משנה means, and agrees that 'their words' means רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier testimonies, something impure is burned together with something else impure. Nothing pure is being made impure. So those testimonies cannot be רבי מאיר's source for burning pure תרומה together with impure. That leaves the dispute of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע as the source.

keyTerms.meaning: A primary source of impurity
A secondary impurity (made impure by an אב)
From the Torah
From their words

phrases.english: And so said Rav Nachman
Rabba bar Avuh said:
Our Mishnah is about a primary impurity by Torah law
and a secondary impurity by Torah law.
And what is 'from their words'?
From the words of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An אמורא's statement that matches the conclusion of steps 10-11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The testimonies involve Torah-level אב and ולד impurity. ״מדבריהם״ means the words of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.

steps.title: רבא objects from רבי יוסי's reply about the meat
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן with a ברייתא. There רבי יוסי argues that the testimonies of 'our Rabbis' do not prove רבי מאיר's rule, starting with the meat case where both pieces are impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raised an objection to רב נחמן: רבי יוסי said, the case being judged is not like the proof. When our Rabbis testified, what did they testify about? If about meat made impure by a ולד הטומאה, which is burned together with meat made impure by an אב הטומאה, then this is impure and that is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a challenge against רב נחמן. רבי יוסי replies to רבי מאיר as if רבי מאיר's source were the testimonies of the Sages, not the dispute of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said the משנה's testimonies deal with Torah-level אב and ולד impurity, and that ״מדבריהם״ means רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. רבא quotes רבי יוסי's full ברייתא, which goes through those same testimonies and ends with what רבי יוסי concedes (step 15). The exact pressure on רב נחמן is spelled out on the next amud. רבי יוסי's first point is that in the meat case both pieces are already impure, so nothing pure is being made impure.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him (from a תנאי source)
The case being judged is not like the proof
They testified
Impure

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is not denying the testimonies. He accepts them, but says they are a different kind of case from burning pure תרומה together with impure.

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to Rav Nachman:
Rabbi Yosei said:
The case being judged is not similar to the proof,
for when our Rabbis testified,
about what did they testify?

phrases.aramaic: אִם עַל הַבָּשָׂר שֶׁנִּטְמָא בִּוְולַד הַטּוּמְאָה
phrases.english: If about meat that became impure through a secondary impurity
that one burns it with meat
that became impure through a primary impurity,
this is impure and that is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's statement in step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's reading that ״מדבריהם״ refers to רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא quotes רבי יוסי's ברייתא about the testimonies, which ends with his concession about ולד and אב impurity (step 15). The challenge to רב נחמן's Torah-level reading builds on that ברייתא and is spelled out on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוסי continues with the oil and lamp case
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי continues: the oil testimony is also no proof, because the oil was only disqualified, not fully pure, when it was lit in an impure lamp.
steps.simpleTranslation: If about oil disqualified by a טבול יום, which one may light in a lamp made impure by someone impure from a corpse, then this is disqualified and that is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the second testimony. רבי יוסי shows that this case also does not involve making something pure become impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil touched by a טבול יום becomes פסול: it is unfit, though not actually impure. Lighting it in an impure lamp only adds impurity to something that was already unfit. Fully pure תרומה being made impure is a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who immersed today but must wait for nightfall to be fully pure
Disqualified (unfit, but not actually impure)
Someone made impure by a corpse
A lamp

phrases.aramaic: אִם עַל הַשֶּׁמֶן שֶׁנִּפְסַל בִּטְבוּל יוֹם
phrases.english: If about oil that was disqualified by a tevul yom
that one may light it in a lamp
that became impure through one impure from a corpse,
this is disqualified and that is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם עַל הַשֶּׁמֶן שֶׁנִּפְסַל בִּטְבוּל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in רבא's objection
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Continues the ברייתא רבא is quoting. Together with step 15's concession, it forms the basis of the challenge to רב נחמן, which is spelled out on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוסי states what he agrees to
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי concedes that תרומה made impure by a ולד הטומאה may be burned together with תרומה made impure by an אב הטומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also agree about תרומה that became impure through a ולד הטומאה, that it may be burned together with תרומה that became impure through an אב הטומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with what רבי יוסי accepts: burning impure with impure. This sets up the point of רבא's challenge, which the גמרא develops next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי allows burning something impure together with something more impure. He does not allow burning pure together with impure. רבא will use this concession to press רב נחמן, who said the testimonies deal with Torah-level אב and ולד impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: We too agree
The portion of produce given to a כהן
One burns

steps.whyThisMatters: This concession is the base of רבא's attack on רב נחמן. The גמרא will ask what רבי יוסי is adding if the testimonies already deal with Torah-level impurity.

phrases.english: We too agree regarding teruma
that became impure through a secondary impurity,
that one may burn it with teruma
that became impure through a primary impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא that רבא quoted, setting up the challenge to רב נחמן
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim about Torah-level impurities and the meaning of ״מדבריהם״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's concession treats impure-with-impure burning as the subject of the testimonies, which sets up a challenge to רב נחמן's reading

steps.title: Doubtful תרומה may not be burned with impure תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי finishes his statement. He rules that תרומה whose status is in doubt (תלויה) may not be burned together with definitely impure תרומה, because אליהו might come and declare it pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how can we burn the doubtful תרומה together with the impure תרומה? Maybe אליהו will come and declare it pure!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of רבי יוסי's ברייתא, which רבא is using to challenge רב נחמן. רבי יוסי explains the one thing he will NOT allow: burning doubtful תרומה together with definitely impure תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the step before, רבי יוסי allowed two kinds of impure תרומה to be burned together, because both are already impure. Doubtful תרומה is different. Its status is not settled, and one day it could be shown to be pure. So burning it with impure תרומה would make possibly-pure תרומה impure by our own hands, and רבי יוסי forbids that.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Hanging' — תרומה whose purity is in doubt and is left undecided
'How can we burn' — a rhetorical way of saying it should not be burned this way
'Perhaps אליהו will come' — a phrase for a doubt that is unresolved now but could be resolved in the future
'And declare it pure' — show that it was really pure all along

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's ruling has two sides. Impure תרומה may be burned with more severely impure תרומה (step 15). Doubtful תרומה may NOT be burned with definitely impure תרומה, because it might really be pure.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Maybe אליהו will come' does not tell a story about אליהו actually coming. It is a set phrase meaning the doubt might be cleared up someday, so we must not treat the item as surely impure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line names the exact case רבי יוסי rejects: burning תלויה with טמאה. Locating his disagreement here is central to how the גמרא works through the dispute and to רבא's challenge against רב נחמן.

phrases.english: But how can we burn
phrases.notes: Rhetorical question meaning 'we may not burn'

phrases.english: the doubtful (תרומה) together with the impure?
phrases.notes: תלויה = status in doubt; טמאה = definitely impure

phrases.english: Perhaps אליהו will come
phrases.notes: The doubt may be resolved in the future

phrases.english: and declare it pure!
phrases.notes: Then we would have made pure תרומה impure for nothing

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הֵיאַךְ נִשְׂרֹף הַתְּלוּיָה עִם הַטְּמֵאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יוסי's statement. Right after granting that lightly impure תרומה may be burned with severely impure תרומה (step 15), he states the limit: doubtful תרומה may not be burned with impure תרומה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's reading (in the name of רבה בר אבוה) of the משנה's testimonies and of ״מדבריהם״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's full ברייתא shows how he reads the testimonies and exactly where he disagrees: he refuses to let doubtful תרומה be burned with impure תרומה. רבא uses this full position to challenge רב נחמן's explanation.
